title: When Agents Say One Thing and Do Another: Validating Elicited Beliefs from LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2602.06286v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes settings where good decisions require forming beliefs over the probability of unknown outcomes. However, it is unclear whether LLMs act as if they hold coherent beliefs when making decisions, or if so, how we could validate models' reports of such beliefs. We propose a decision-theoretic framework that elicits both probability judgments and decisions from an agent and tests their mutual consistency. Formally, our methods characterize whether it is possible for the actions to be produced by a ``near-rational" decision maker who holds the elicited probability as their true belief. We show that, perhaps surprisingly, this formalization implies empirically testable conditions even without any assumption about the agent's utility function. Applying our framework to stylized clinical diagnosis tasks, we find that models' reported beliefs are demonstrably imperfect summar

translated_title: 当智能体言行不一时：验证从大语言模型中引导出的信念
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被部署在高风险场景中，在这些场景下，良好的决策需要对未知结果的概率形成信念。然而，目前尚不清楚LLM在决策时是否表现得好像持有连贯一致的信念，如果是的话，我们又该如何验证模型对这类信念的报告。我们提出了一个决策理论框架，该框架从智能体处同时引导出概率判断和决策行为，并检验二者之间的相互一致性。从形式上讲，我们的方法刻画了这些行为是否有可能由一个将所引导出的概率视为其真实信念的“近理性”决策者所产生。我们表明，或许令人惊讶的是，即使不对智能体的效用函数做任何假设，这种形式化也蕴含了可以经验检验的条件。将我们的框架应用于程式化的临床诊断任务，我们发现模型所报告的信念被证明是不完美的总结。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个决策理论框架，在不假设效用函数的前提下检验大语言模型所报告的概率判断与其决策行为之间的相互一致性，并发现模型的信念报告与其真实决策行为存在明显不一致。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a decision-theoretic framework that tests the mutual consistency between LLMs' elicited probability judgments and their decisions—without any utility function assumptions—and finds that models' reported beliefs are demonstrably inconsistent with their actual decision-making behavior.
